# Vegetation-Specific Slicing
## Overview
Vegetation-Specific Slicing is a family of rendering techniques for plant structures that replaces high-complexity polygonal meshes with image-based representations to achieve real-time performance [S1]. It sets itself apart from general texture slicing by decomposing vegetation into structural components (solid meshes versus sparse planar slices) and leveraging hardware compositing for efficient transparency accumulation [S1].
## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Fiber Surface Texturing](5672-fiber-surface-texturing.md)
Fiber Surface Texturing is a method for visualizing fiber fields on tetrahedral meshes by mapping fiber path parameters to 1D textures [see Fiber Surface Texturing](5672-fiber-surface-texturing.md). It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Regular Texcell Slicing with Non-Linear Pre-filtering](9823-regular-texcell-slicing-with-non-linear-pre-filtering.md) by using 1D texture lookups driven by global fiber path length rather than 2D alpha-blended slices, allowing for efficient representation of continuous fiber trajectories across complex mesh boundaries [see Fiber Surface Texturing](5672-fiber-surface-texturing.md). Choose it when rendering sparse, directional data (fibers) within volumetric elements [see Fiber Surface Texturing](5672-fiber-surface-texturing.md).

### [Regular Texcell Slicing with Non-Linear Pre-filtering](9823-regular-texcell-slicing-with-non-linear-pre-filtering.md)
Regular Texcell Slicing is a vegetation-specific volume rendering technique that represents forest canopies as a stack of ground-parallel planar slices (texcells) stored in a 2D texture pyramid [see Regular Texcell Slicing with Non-Linear Pre-filtering](9823-regular-texcell-slicing-with-non-linear-pre-filtering.md). It sets itself apart from sibling methods that may use explicit geometry or 3D textures by relying on pre-computed 2D alpha-premultiplied textures blended offline to create coarser LODs, ensuring correct transparency accumulation and efficient hardware rendering [see Regular Texcell Slicing with Non-Linear Pre-filtering](9823-regular-texcell-slicing-with-non-linear-pre-filtering.md). Choose it for large-scale forest scenes requiring efficient Level of Detail (LOD) management and filtering [see Regular Texcell Slicing with Non-Linear Pre-filtering](9823-regular-texcell-slicing-with-non-linear-pre-filtering.md).

### Slicing and Blending for Vegetation Rendering
A simplified image-based rendering approach for vegetation that uses alpha-blended textured polygons to represent sparse parts (twigs and leaves) as a set of parallel planar layers called slices, while using ordinary mesh-based rendering for solid parts (trunk and limbs) [S1]. It renders dozens of detailed trees in real-time with off-the-shelf hardware, providing significantly improved image quality over existing real-time techniques [S1]. Rendering from an arbitrary viewpoint in a 360-degree circle around the tree center is achieved by blending between the nearest two slicings [S1]. In implementation, only 6 slicings with 5 slices each are sufficient to visualize a tree for a moving or stationary observer with perceptually similar quality to the original model [S1].

## Background
The techniques within this family address the challenges of interactive 3D rendering of vegetation, which is computationally expensive due to large geometric complexity even for simple plants [S1]. The foundational work on "Slicing and Blending for Vegetation Rendering" was introduced to provide a simplified image-based rendering approach based on the limitations of human perception of complex geometry [S1]. This allows for real-time rendering of dozens of detailed trees using standard hardware [S1]. The specific methods for fiber surface texturing and regular texcell slicing extend these principles to handle specific data structures, as detailed in [Fiber Surface Texturing](5672-fiber-surface-texturing.md) and [Regular Texcell Slicing with Non-Linear Pre-filtering](9823-regular-texcell-slicing-with-non-linear-pre-filtering.md).
